text: We evaluated a contrastive pretext objective applied for 500 steps before weak-label fine-tuning, using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and mistral-7b as the strong student, across 6 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.51 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.84, with the weak-to-strong transfer model attaining 0.55 accuracy (SE 0.04). The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.13 with a standard error of 0.12, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.41. The measured PGR therefore falls below the baseline and carries an error bar large enough that it is not distinguishable from a wide range of values, so these data provide no evidence that the pretext objective helps; if anything, the point estimate runs in the opposite direction. Given the six-seed sample and the size of the standard error, we draw no directional conclusion about the method's effect and recommend more seeds before interpreting this comparison further.
